properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an ice jam continues.

* WHERE...Pilot Station.

* WHEN...Until 100 AM AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- As of 7 PM Saturday,the breakup front was located
approximately 12 miles downriver of Mountain Village. It is
moving slowly into the remaining in-place ice. Plenty of high
water is still pushing down the river from the jam near Holy
Cross a few days ago. As the surge of high water moves
downstream, it is causing flooding in several communities
along the Yukon.

- As of Sunday morning, water levels are continuing to rise
following significant rises on Saturday. Low-lying areas were
flooded. Water levels have exceeded 2024 and are second only
to 1989. Water levels could continue to rise slowly until the
breakup front moves farther downstream. Residents should
continue to exercise caution in and around flood waters.
- For Yukon River at Pilot Station:
At 10:45am the stage was 33.6 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/aprfc
properties.instruction:

television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued May 24 at 11:38AM AKDT until May 26 at 1:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by ice jams, high water, and heavy ice runs
continues to be possible.

* WHERE...Lower Yukon River. This includes the communities of
Alakanuk, Emmonak, Kotlik, and Mountain Village.

* WHEN...Through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...High water may result in flooding of rivers, creeks,
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- As of Saturday evening, the River Watch Team reports the
breakup front is approximately 12 miles downstream of
Mountain Village. They observed local breakup at Emmonak and
Alakanuk with ice moving steadily through those communities.
As the breakup front works its way downstream Sunday into
Monday, residents in Nunam Iqua, Alakanuk, and Emmonak should
follow its progress closely. There is a long stretch of very
high water with abundant chunk ice behind the front that
should arrive in the next 2-3 days. Based on water levels
seen at the gauge at Pilot Station, these communities could
see the highest water levels since 1989.

- Http://www.weather.gov/aprfc

to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued May 24 at 3:37PM EDT until May 24 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 3 to 6 feet
in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Eastern Monmouth and Coastal Ocean.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday evening.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Always obey posted Beach Flags. If you enter the surf zone,
always have a floatation device with you and swim near a
lifeguard if possible. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float and do not swim against the current. If able, swim parallel
to the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or
wave for help.

sure you listen to emergency services. Visit ready.gov/plan for

that promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-
threatening. This does not mean there is a fire. These conditions
are either occurring now or will begin soon. It is important to
have multiple ways to receive information from authorities.

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued May 24 at 12:05PM MDT until May 25 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS Boise ID
properties.description:
...GUSTY RANGELAND WINDS AHEAD OF COLD FRONT...

Continued warm and very dry conditions ahead of a cold front on
the afternoon and evening of Memorial Day could create a critical
fire weather pattern as pre-frontal winds increase. Following
conditions tomorrow we will see good RH recovery overnight with a
30-40% chance of wetting rains through the rest of the week.

The National Weather Service in Boise has issued a Fire Weather
Watch for winds and low relative humidities, which is in effect
from Monday afternoon through Monday evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Oregon, Fire Weather Zone 672 Southern
Grasslands.

* TIMING...From Monday afternoon through Monday evening.

* WINDS...Southwest 20 to 25 mph with gusts up to 40 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...11 to 15 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...80 to 88 degrees.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are possible. Listen for later forecasts and possible Red Flag
Warnings.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 12:25PM EDT by NWS Gray ME
properties.description:
* Temperatures this Holiday weekend may cause people to
underestimate the dangers of the cold water temperatures which are
currently only in the mid 50s across Sebago Lake and Lake
Winnipesaukee, and in the mid 50s in the regions smaller lakes and
rivers.

* The cold water temperatures can quickly cause hypothermia to
anyone immersed in the water. When the water temperature is below
60 degrees, the average submerged person could loose dexterity
within minutes and be unable to accomplish simple tasks. Anyone
on small boats, canoes, or kayaks should plan accordingly if
recreating this weekend and use extreme caution to avoid this
threat. Paddle smart from the start and always wear your life
jacket!

* Winds will be breezy this afternoon with some gusts up to 25 mph
across parts of the area. If boating on large bodies of water,
these strong winds can increase the likelihood of overturning
your boat, canoe, or kayak due to increased wave heights.

at a site along or near the banks of rivers or streams, move away
from those locations and seek higher ground. Trails in hilly terrain
can quickly become unstable during or shortly after heavy rainfall.

Portage and hiking trails may be impassable and low-lying campsites
may be inundated with excessive runoff in this section of the
Boundary Waters as flooding is occurring or imminent.

enforcement and to the National Weather Service in Duluth when you
can do so safely. Flooding can be reported to the National Weather
Service at 1-800-685-8612.

properties.areaDesc: Unalaska and Nikolski
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 5:04AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
An unseasonably strong storm system for this time of year will
bring strong winds and gusts to Nikolski, Unalaska, and Akutan
beginning early this evening. Expect winds to quickly increase
this afternoon with sustained southeasterly winds of 20 to 35 mph
with gusts of 45 to 60 mph, becoming more southerly by Monday
morning. Winds will likely peak overnight tonight into Monday
morning before slowly diminishing through late Monday afternoon.
As the storm moves east of the area Monday evening, winds will
shift, becoming southwesterly with gusts of 35 to 45 mph likely
through Wednesday before finally winding down.

NWSheadline: UNSEASONABLY STRONG WINDS FROM EARLY THIS EVENING THROUGH MONDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Pribilof Islands
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 5:04AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
An unseasonably strong storm system for this time of year will
bring strong winds and gusts to the Pribilof Islands beginning
late this evening. Expect winds to quickly increase late this
afternoon with sustained easterly winds of 20 to 35 mph with gusts
of 45 to 60 mph, becoming more northeasterly by Monday evening.
Snow or rain/snow may produce areas of blowing snow at times
overnight tonight. Winds will likely peak early Monday morning
before slowly diminishing through late Monday evening. As the
storm moves east of the area Monday evening, winds will shift,
becoming northwesterly with gusts of 35 to 45 mph likely through
Wednesday before finally winding down.

NWSheadline: UNSEASONABLY STRONG WINDS FROM LATE THIS EVENING THROUGH MONDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Aleutians East Borough
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 5:04AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
An unseasonably strong storm system for this time of year will
bring strong winds and gusts from Akutan to Sand Point and Nelson
Lagoon to beginning overnight tonight into early Monday morning.
Expect winds to quickly increase after midnight with sustained
southeasterly winds of 20 to 35 mph with gusts of 45 to 60 mph,
becoming more southerly by Monday afternoon. Gusts to 70 mph are
possible for Cold Bay Monday morning. Winds will likely peak by
mid morning Monday morning before slowly diminishing through
Monday night. As the storm moves east of the area Tuesday morning,
winds will shift, becoming westerly with gusts of 35 to 45 mph
likely through Wednesday before finally winding down.

NWSheadline: UNSEASONABLY STRONG WINDS FROM EARLY MONDAY MORNING THROUGH MONDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Atka and Adak
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 5:04AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
An unseasonably strong storm system for this time of year will
bring strong winds and gusts to Adak and Atka beginning early
this morning. Expect winds to quickly increase after sunrise
this with sustained easterly winds of 30 to 45 mph with gusts of
50 to 65 mph. Winds will likely peak around mid afternoon before
slowly diminishing through late tonight. There will be lull in
the strong winds overnight tonight into Monday morning before
winds shift to the northwest and increase in intensity. Expect
northwest winds 20 to 35 mph with gusts up to 50 mph late Monday
morning through Monday evening. This second round of gusty winds
will slowly diminish overnight Monday into Tuesday before finally
winding down by Tuesday night.

NWSheadline: UNSEASONABLY STRONG WINDS FROM EARLY THIS MORNING THROUGH MONDAY EVENING

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 5:55AM EDT by NWS Caribou ME
properties.description:
* The warm air temperatures this weekend in the mid 60s to low
70s may cause people to underestimate the dangers of the cold
water temperatures which are currently only around 50 degrees on
Moosehead Lake and in the middle to upper 50s on smaller lakes
and rivers.

* The cold water temperatures can quickly cause hypothermia to
anyone immersed in the water. According to the Maine Warden
Service, when the water temperature is below 60 degrees, the
average submerged person could lose dexterity within minutes and
be unable to accomplish simple tasks. Anyone on small boats,
canoes or kayaks should plan accordingly if recreating this
weekend and use extreme caution to avoid this threat. Paddle
smart from the start and always wear your life jacket!

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 4:50PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
A tropical disturbance, known as JTWC's Invest 99W, is currently
centered near 6N142E, just west of Eauripik. Although 99W remains
broad and disorganized, convection has rapidly improved over the last
day. Invest 99W is also connected to the monsoon trough to the
south, bringing a fresh surge of westerly winds, which will allow it
to organize. This convective structure is leading to a large area of
numerous to widespread showers and isolated thunderstorms, and choppy
seas across Chuuk and Yap State. Invest 99W remains rated sub-low by
the JTWC, which means development into a significant tropical
cyclone is not expected within the next few days.

As Invest 99W lifts northward this week, a monsoon tail will
intensify on the south side. Westerly to southwesterly winds of 20 to
30 kts will be possible along with seas hazardous to small craft.
Guidance continues to show this region as a narrow band displaced
from both Yap's and Palau's coastal waters, with seas remaining below
10 feet through Wednesday. As the system shifts further away, the
monsoon tail may transition into an inflow tail with southerly flow.
This could bring seas near hazardous conditions to Yap's coastal
waters late this week.

Residents and mariners should monitor the latest forecasts for the
region at weather.gov/gum/PublicForecasts and any information shared
by WSO Palau, WSO Yap, and WSO Chuuk for the local regions. For more
information on Invest 99W, see bulletins issued by JTWC under WMO
header ABPW10 PGTW and WTPN21 PGTW.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an ice jam continues.

* WHERE...Mountain Village.

* WHEN...Until 100 AM AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1020 PM AKDT, the breakup front was located approximately
12 miles downriver of Mountain Village as of 7 PM Saturday.
It is moving slowly into the remaining in-place ice. Plenty
of high water is still pushing down the river from the jam
near Holy Cross a few days ago. As the surge of high water
moves downstream, it is causing flooding in several
communities along the Yukon.

- A local observer in Mountain Village reports the water rose
several feet on Saturday. Ice continues to run bank to bank
with the primary outlet on the south side of the Yukon. Until
the breakup front moves farther downstream Sunday, expect
continued slow rises and potential flooding of low-lying
areas.
- For Yukon River at Pilot Station:
At 9:45pm the stage was 32.6 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/aprfc
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

properties.instruction:

from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
An unseasonably strong storm system for this time of year will
bring strong winds and gusts from Akutan to Sand Point and Nelson
Lagoon to beginning overnight Sunday into early Monday morning.
Expect winds to quickly increase after midnight with sustained
southeasterly winds of 20 to 35 mph with gusts of 45 to 60 mph,
becoming more southerly by Monday afternoon. Gusts to 70 mph are
possible for Cold Bay Monday morning. Winds will likely peak
by mid morning Monday morning before slowly diminishing through
Monday night. As the storm moves east of the area Tuesday morning,
winds will shift, becoming westerly with gusts of 35 to 45 mph
likely through Wednesday before finally winding down.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 23 at 1:40PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
An unseasonably strong storm system for this time of year will
bring strong winds and gusts to Adak and Atka beginning early
Sunday morning. Expect winds to quickly increase after sunrise
Sunday with sustained easterly winds of 30 to 45 mph with gusts of
50 to 65 mph. Winds will likely peak around mid afternoon before
slowly diminishing through late Sunday night. There will be a lull
in the strong winds overnight Sunday into Monday morning before
winds shift to the northwest and increase in intensity. Expect
northwest winds 20 to 35 mph with gusts up to 50 mph late Monday
morning through Monday evening. This second round of gusty winds
will slowly diminish overnight Monday into Tuesday before finally
winding down by Tuesday night.

properties.areaDesc: Big Horn, MT; Carbon, MT; Park, MT; Stillwater, MT; Sweet Grass, MT; Yellowstone, MT; Sheridan, WY
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued May 23 at 1:44AM MDT by NWS Billings MT
properties.description:
ESFBYZ

Unseasonably warm temperatures this weekend into early next week will
result in higher flows on area waterways through next week as the
remaining high elevation snowpack melts. Flooding is not expected at
this time. Rivers such as the Yellowstone and Clarks Fork of the
Yellowstone, Stillwater, and Boulder are expected to see flows double
the current rates by late in the week.

Smaller streams and creeks flowing out of the mountains will see
rises late this weekend into early next week, with larger rivers and
streams further downstream seeing the strongest increases from
Tuesday through Friday.

Those with interests along foothills waterways should be prepared for
higher water levels, and move property and livestock away from
rivers, streams, and low lying areas.

Recreationists in the mountains and foothills should be prepared for
changing conditions and use extra caution when near waterways. Flows
will be higher and faster, and the water is very cold. Cloudy water
conditions during runoff can also hide submerged hazards. Keep
children and pets away from the edge of fast flowing waterways.

Stay tuned to the forecast. Please report any flooding to local law
enforcement and have them relay the report to the National Weather
Service.
